lines: Peace to you. The barley is late and my knees are early. If you hear anything worth the walk, come and tell an old man.

annotate.text: Ezra says the words remind him of the prophet Isaiah.
Ezra says what Hannah describes puts him in mind of Isaiah's 'voice in the wilderness'.

lines: You have been listening to the road talk, I see. Sit a moment.
A man crying in the wilderness, baptizing in the Jordan, saying the kingdom of heaven is at hand. I have turned it over since morning.

The prophet Isaiah wrote: 'The voice of him that crieth in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.' I do not say this John is anything. I say the words came to mind, and they have not left.
If I knew that, I would be a rich teacher in Jerusalem and not an old man with bad knees.
Go and see, if your heart tells you to. Go with open eyes, and come back and tell me what you saw.
Have you been to the river? No? Then why are you standing in front of an old man's door? Go and see. Come back and tell me.
Wait a moment. The road to the Jordan is long, and not everyone you will meet on it is an honest traveler.
Take this. It was mine when I was young and the roads were worse. For protection on the road.
Keep it sheathed unless you must. A sword answers a danger. It does not answer a question.

choices.text: I will carry it carefully. Thank you, Elder.
Is it truly mine to keep?

lines: It has hung on my wall for forty years, doing nothing but gathering dust and reproach. Better it walks than hangs.
Now go. Come back and tell me what you saw.
One thing more, and then I will let you go. You heard me give you Isaiah's words. There is a good deal more written than Isaiah.
When something strange happens, I do not ask first what it means. I ask what was written before it. The Law, the Prophets, the Psalms are a long memory, and what I cannot recall I go and look up.
If you come across an old scroll, on the road or in the grass, bring it to me. My eyes are poor, but I can still read the Hebrew, and I will tell you what it says. What it means, I will leave to you.

choices.text: Where would I find such a scroll?
I will keep my eyes open.

lines: Scrolls are lost, sold, hidden in a hayloft and forgotten. A careless traveler drops one; a widow sells her husband's. I cannot tell you where. That is why one looks.
Look under things. Look where people do not.
Hand it here. Slowly, slowly. Ah. Malachi, the last of the Twelve.

He wrote: 'Behold, I will send my messenger, and he shall prepare the way before me: and the LORD, whom ye seek, shall suddenly come to his temple, even the messenger of the covenant, whom ye delight in: behold, he shall come, saith the LORD of hosts.'
And near the end of the book: 'Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD.'
I do not tell you who the messenger is. Men have argued it for four hundred years. I tell you only what is written. Set it beside what you have heard, and see whether the two sit well together.
The books of the Kings. Let me find the place. Here.
The king asked his men what manner of man had met them. They answered, 'He was an hairy man, and girt with a girdle of leather about his loins.' And the king said, 'It is Elijah the Tishbite.'
You have been telling me what Hannah saw, and I see why you brought this. But a leather girdle is what poor men and wilderness men wear. Do not make too much of a garment.
